A.B. M Nurul Islam, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-record ------ For the Appellants. 
Mustafa Niaz Mohammad, Advocate, instructed by Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-record ------ For the Respondents.
parties:
Md. Yousuf and others ------ Appellants
Vs.
Administrator of Waqf, Government of Bangladesh, 4, New Eskaton Road, Dhaka and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Amin J :- This is a writ petitioners appeal, by leave, against the judgment of March 1, 2003 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 171 of 2003 discharging the Rule obtained impugning the other of June, 10, 2002 of the Office of the Administrator of Waqfs directing the District Magistrate, Chittagong for taking action as per provision of section 64 (1) of the Waqfs Ordinance, 1962 (the Ordinance) for evicting the writ-petitioners from the respective shops, taken lease by the written agreement from the Mutawalli, treating them as trespassers in respect of the property of Mowlana Abdur Rashid Waqf Estate and to make over possession of the property to the official Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate. 

 2. Facts, in short, that the writ petitioners are the monthly tenants of Waqf Estate on the basis of the written agreement in the respective shops which are semi pucca structures, that Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate refused to accept rent on November 19, 2001 and thereupon the tenants of the respective shops sent rent by postal money order and that the Mutawalli having had refused to accept the money so sent through postal money order the tenants i. e the writ petitioners started depositing rent in the Court of House Rent Controller and the rent till now. At that stage the Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate filed a petition to the Administrator of Waqfs for taking action for the eviction of the tenants in the light of the Provision of section 64(1) of the Ordinance and thereupon the Administrator of Waqfs wrote the letter impugned in the writ petition to the District Magistrate, Chittagong for evicting the writ petitioners describing them as trespassers from their respective shops. The District Magistrate on receipt of the said letter of the Administrator of Waqfs Started Miscellaneous Case No. 28 of 2002 under the provision of Government and Local Authority Lands and Buildings (Recovery of Possession) Ordinance, 1970 (Ordinance No. 24 of 1970) on 28.8.2002 for the eviction of the writ petitions but the same did not reach finality. 

 3. The writ petition was filed contending that the writ petitioners are neither unauthorized occupants of the shops in the Waqf property nor trespassers in respect of the property of the Waqf Estate and as such they are not liable to be evicted as per provision of section 64(1) of the Ordinance, that they being the tenants in the property of the Waqf Estate and their tenancy having not been terminated in compliance of the law they are not liable to the evicted from Their respective shops even under the provision of the House Rent Control Act, 1991 (Act No. 3 of 1991), (the Act), the action of the Administrator of Waqfs for evicting the writ-petitioners from their respective shops is illegal and without lawful authority. 

 4. The Rule was opposed by the Respondent No. 5, Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate stating amongst others that structures wherein the writ petitioners are running shops were not erected by the writ petitioners that the structures were made by the Mutawalli, that the writ petitioners are not the tenants of the Waqf Estate but they are trespassers in the Waqf property, that although they were tenants but they having had defaulted in the payment of rent regularly, are no longer the tenants of the Waqf Estate, that the cases have been filed in the Court of House Rent Controller only to continue unauthorized occupation of the Waqf property, that the writ-petitioners by their unauthorized occupation of the Waqf property created obstruction in the development of the Waqf property by way of making construction as per plan approved by the Municipality, that the order of the Administrator of Waqfs for eviction of the writ petitioners is quite legal and that the same has been made quite in accordance with the provision of section 64(1) of the Ordinance, that Miscellaneous Case No. 28 of 2002 started by the Additional Deputy Commissioner for eviction of the writ petitioners is quite legal, that the writ petition is not maintainable since in pursuant to the order of the Administrator of Waqfs the Additional Deputy Commissioner has started the Miscellaneous Case No. 28 of 2002 for the eviction of the writ petitioners and that final order has been passed on 11.10.2002 for eviction of the writ-petitioners, that order of the Administrator of Waqfs being appeasable one as per provision of section 64(2) of the Ordinance, the writ petition is not maintainable. 

 5. The High Court Division discharged the Rule upon observing since the Administrator of Waqfs being satisfied about the creation of disturbance/obstruction by the writ-petitioners in the peaceful management of the Waqf property made the order impugned in the writ petition asking the Deputy Commissioner to evict the writ petitioners in the background of specific allegation of creating disturbance and putting obstruction by refusing to vacate the property of the Waqf Estate and thus there by the writ petitioners as are standing in the way of development of the Waqf property and that "their action tantamount to disturb/obstruct in the peaceful management of the in question and, therefore, the administrator applied to the Deputy Commissioner under section 64(1) of the Ordinance by the impugned Memo. Dated 10.6.2002, which, in our view, does not suffer from any illegality or it can be said to have been made without lawful authority and as such we do not find that the Administrator of Waqfs committed any illegality in issuing the aforesaid Memo Dated 10.6.2002. 

 8. The learned Counsel appearing for the appellants has submitted that they being the tenants of the Waqf Estate, as such they do not come within the mischief of the provision of section 64(1) of the Ordinance and that the provision of Section 64(1) of the Ordinance. has no manner of application since the appellants neither trespassers nor strangers in the Waqf property and that they are staying in the Waqf property under the agreement of monthly tenancy and that they having not defaulted in the payment of rent and consequent thereupon as they remain tenants of Waqf Estate they cannot be considered strangers or trespassers in the Waqf property. It has also been contended on behalf of the appellants that the action of the Additional Deputy Commissioner in initiating Miscellaneous Case No. 28 of 2002 in the light of the letter dated 10.6.2002 of the Administrator of Waqfs is illegal since provision of Government and Local Authority lands and Buildings (Recovery of Possession) Ordinance, 1970, hereinafter referred to as the Ordinance No. 24 of 1970, has no manner of application in respect of the property of the Waqf Estate, that the appellants being the tenants in the Waqf Estate they can only be evicted from the premises in their occupation as tenants upon resorting to the provisions of House Rent Controller Act, 1991, that in view of the terms and conditions of the tenancy agreement the Mutawallli of the Waqf Estate is estopped from evicting the appellants without payment of damages and without making provision for appellants accommodation in the building claimed to be constructed in the Waqf Estate. It has also been contended on behalf of the appellants that the Mutawalli has approached the Administration of Waqfs for the eviction of the appellants at the maneuvering of the person mentioned at serial Nos. 2 and 3 of the letter of the Administrator of Waqfs dated 10.6.2002 for the illegal gain of the said persons. 

 10. The appellants are the tenants in respect of the Waqf property under the tenancy agreement between the respective shop owners and the Mutaqalli of the Waqf Estate. 

 12. The fact of entry of the appellants in the Waqf property as tenants of the Waqf Estate is not dispute. It is the contention of the Respondent No. 5 that the tenants have violated the terms and conditions of the tenancy agreement in defaulting to pay the rent as per tenancy agreement. Suffice it to say the Respondent No. 5 has not denied the contention of the appellants that the Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate having had refused to accept the rent, the tenants are depositing the rent in the Court. It may be mentioned when the Mutawalli approached the Administrator of Waqfs for eviction of the appellants from the Waqf property no material was placed before the Administrator of Waqfs that tenancy of the appellants having had been terminated they are illegally staying in the property of the Waqf Estate. At the time of hearing of the appeal no material has been brought on record to show that the tenancy of the appellants have been terminated. It appears the Respondent No. 5 has consciously avoided to proceed against the appellants in the light of the provision of House Rent Control Act, 1991. Rather the Mutaqalli chose summary procedure, for eviction of the appellants calling them strangers to and trespassers in the property of the Waqf Estate. 

 13. The learned Counsel for the Respondent No. 5 has submitted that the appellants are trespassers on the Waqf property since they are neither "beneficiary" as has been defined in section 2(2) nor "person interested" in a Waqf property as has been defined in Section 2(8) of the Ordinance and consequently they are strangers to the Waqf as has been defined in section 2(9) of the Ordinance and that they having had created disturbance and obstruction in the peaceful management of the Waqf property and that also disturbing the possession of the Waqf property by the Mutaqalli, the Mutawalli had quite legally approached the Administrator of Waqfs for the eviction of the appellants as per provision of section 64(1) of the Ordinance. It has also been contended on behalf of the Respondent No. 5 that the appellants being trespassers on the property of the Waqf Estate the Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate quite correctly approached the Administrator of Waqfs and the Administrator of Waqf had quite legally passed the order under section 64(1) of the Ordinance. 

 Person interested in the Waqf Estate has been defined as: 

 16. In the background of the aforesaid provisions of the Ordinance it has been submitted that except a co-sharer of the waqf property or an individual beneficiary or a person interested in a waqf property, all other persons being stranger to the waqf property they are liable to be evicted as per provision of section 64(1) of the Ordinance and that the appellants being not any one of the category of persons as mentioned hereinabove i.e. co-sharer, beneficiary or person interested in the waqf property and that their stay in the waqf property being that of the person of the category of stranger the Administrator of waqfs has legally passed the order for their eviction as per section 64(1) of the Ordinance. The learned Counsel for the Respondent No. 5 also submitted that the appellants having had violated the terms and conditions of the tenancy agreement they became trespassers on the property of the Waqf Estate and as such they are liable to be evicted as ordered by the Administrator of Waqfs. 

 18. So it is seen that the expression "stranger to Waqf” is to be read in the light of the definition person interested in a Waqf' as has been given in sub-section 8 of section 2 of the Ordinance. Having eye on the definition of "person interested in a Waqf” the appellants status with which they came over the Waqf property and staying there till today are not "person interested in a Waqf" although temporarily some of them may be "person interested in a Waqf” while they are saying prayer or performing any religious rite in a mosque etc. The position of the appellants in the light of the definition in section 2(9) of the Ordinance of the "stranger to Waqf" does not come within the category of person stranger to the Waqf property. Now the question are the appellants trespassers on the Waqf property. The accepted position is that the appellants are the tenants of the Waqf Estate under written agreement. This being the position it cannot be said that the appellants stay on the land of Waqf is that of trespasser. In the background of the materials on record it cannot be said that although their entry at the initial was lawful but later on their stay in the waqf property is unlawful. The appellants are the tenants of the Waqf Estate. Their case is that the Mutawalli having had declined to accept the rent they after due compliance of the provision of law are depositing the rent in the Court of House Rent Controller. As stated earlier the Mutawalli has not terminated the tenancy of the appellants on any of the grounds as in the premises Rent Control Act or in the Transfer of Property Act. This being the position we are of the view that the appellants being not trespassers on the land of the Waqf Estate they are not liable to be evicted from their respective shops upon resorting to the provision of Section 64(1) of the Ordinance. 

 19. It has been contended by the Respondent No. 5 that the Waqf Estate has undertaken scheme for the development of the Waqf property including the premises in which the appellants have their shops and that as part of such development scheme the Waqf Estate has got a plan approved from the Municipality for making new construction. 

 20. The terms and conditions of the agreement of tenancy as quoted hereinbefore clearly make the provision for meeting a situation as likely to arise in the event of implementing the scheme of the Waqf Estate and as such there was no necessity of approaching the Administrator of Waqfs for taking action under Section 64(1) of the Ordinance. It has been contended from the side of the Respondent No. 5 that attempts were made to mutually tackle the situation but the appellants were unwilling to accommodate the Waqf Estate for under taking the development work. If this contention is accepted as correct, then too the Waqf Estate or that the Administrator of Waqfs is not legally competent to resort to the provision of section 64(1) of the Ordinance for-summary eviction of the appellants who are the monthly tenants of the Waqf Estate. There are sufficient provisions in the law regulating relationship of the landlord and tenant. as the appellants are and also providing remedy to the landlord to get the possession of the rented premises in the different situations particularly in the situation as the Waqf Estate claims i. e undertaking of development scheme including the construction of a new buildings in rented premises. 

 21. The undenied position is that the Waqf Estate has not terminated the tenancy agreement between the appellants and the Waqf Estate at any point of time, either prior to approaching the Administrator of Waqfs for taking action under section 64(1) of the Ordinance or subsequent thereto. It is seen from the terms and conditions of the agreement of tenancy that there is stipulation in the said agreement of tenancy to the effect that the waqf estate in case of new construction would accommodate the persons like the appellants in the newly constructed buildings. In the background of the materials on the record it is seen that appellants entry on the land in suit was not of a trespasser, rather the appellants came over the land upon having offer from the waqf estate for coming over the land of the waqf Estate. 

 22. The contention of the Respondent No. 5 that the appellants are strangers also appears to be not well conceived since they came in the waqf property upon executing since they came in the waqf property upon executing agreement of monthly tenancy in favour of the Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate. 

 23. Since the appellants are neither strangers nor trespassers as regard the waqf property, rather being the tenants of the Waqf Estate and the said tenancy having not been terminated the order of the Administrator of Waqf for eviction of the appellants as per provision of section 64(1) of the Ordinance cannot be considered as legal, rather the said order is a misconceived one. As the appellants are tenants of the waqf estate and that even if the tenancy is terminated, the appellants are not liable to be evicted resorting to provision of section 64(1) of the ordinance since the relationship between the appellants and the waqf estate is governed by the provision of premises Rent Control Act, 1991. 

 24. It is seen from the materials on record that on receiving the letter of Administrator of Waqf for eviction of the appellants in the background of the provision of section 64(1) of the Ordinance the Deputy Commissioner initiated a Miscellaneous case being Miscellaneous Case No. 28 of 2002 under the provision of the Government and Local Authority Lands and Buildings Recovery of Possession Ordinance, 1970 (Ordinance No. 24 of 1970). In our view the Miscellaneous Case so initiated by the Deputy Commissioner under the provision of ordinance No. 24 of 1970 was not legal since provisions of the Ordinance No. 24 of 1970 relate to the Government land and buildings and that by notification the provisions of the said Ordinance may be extended to in respect of the local authorities mentioned in the notification. The waqf property certainly not being the land of the Government or the construction standing in such property being not the category of the structure as contemplates by the provision of the Ordinance No. 24 of 1970 and moreover the Waqf Estate is not being a local authority initiation of the Miscellaneous case under the provision of the ordinance No. 24 of 1970 by the Deputy commissioner and the making order of eviction of the appellants were not legal. The provision of section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance itself authorizes the Deputy Commissioner to evict the person mentioned therein on being asked by the Administrator of Waqfs. No separate proceeding under any law need be initiated for eviction of the occupier of the Waqf property in the background of the provision of Section 64 (1) of the Ordinance. 

 25. It is seen from the letter of the Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate addressed to the Administrator of Waqfs that he approached the Administrator of Waqfs that he approached the Administrator of Waqfs for making order for the eviction of the “অস্থায়ী দোকান ভাড়াটিয়াদের” as per provision of section 64(1) of the Waqfs Ordinance. As has already been stated earlier that the relationship between the monthly ejectable tenant(s) and the landlord (s) is governed by the premises and Rent Control Act, 1991. In our view provision of section 64(1) of the Ordinance has never been intended to deal with the monthly ejectable tenants of the Waqf Estate. Suffice it to say the provision of section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance is applicable in respect of the persons as mentioned in the said section in the background of the facts and situations as have been stipulated therein and not in respect of the monthly ejectable tenant of the waqf estate. As such the order of the Waqf Administrator passed under section 64(1) of the Ordinance for eviction of the appellants, who are the monthly ejectable tenants of the Waqf Estate, was not legally well conceived one, rather the said order has been passed in respect of the matters not conversed by the provision of section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance.
